reference.description: Existing production fixed-step Leapfrog KDK schedule

candidate.description: Bounded scheduling model with immutable time bins and synchronized ownership

workloads.definition: Four time bins repeated over a deterministic two-rank ownership pattern
Fast particles clustered in one half and slow particles in the other half
Heterogeneous bins with all particles migrating at a synchronization boundary

semantics.time_bin: bin b executes on base tick t when t modulo 2^b is zero
semantics.ownership: one owner per particle; owner changes only at synchronization ticks
semantics.synchronization: global schedule boundary every eight base ticks
semantics.migration: ownership migration is applied at tick 32 before the next active work list
semantics.rollback: restore tick, ownership, counters, and event hash before retry
semantics.restart: resume from a captured schedule state without replaying earlier events

decision.reason: No production block-force path or end-to-end speedup is justified by this scheduling-only qualification
promotion_requires: measured end-to-end gain over fixed KDK

proxy_policy.modeled_speedup: fixed event count divided by block event count
proxy_policy.timing: scheduler loop wall time only; not an end-to-end simulation benchmark
proxy_policy.conservation: particle ledger and ownership conservation only; physical energy remains covered by fixed KDK tests

invariants: fixed KDK remains the only production integrator
block active work is sorted by stable particle index
time-bin intervals are bounded to powers of two from zero through three
migration occurs only at a synchronization boundary
restart and rollback reproduce the uninterrupted block schedule exactly
the input workload is not mutated by qualification
the candidate is not promoted without a physical end-to-end result
